text:
Systematic review and network meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42022315497) comparing single-shot ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia techniques against placebo or no intervention for postoperative opioid consumption in adults undergoing open cardiac surgery with median sternotomy. Fifteen randomized studies with 849 patients were included, with risk-of-bias assessment and GRADE-style appraisal of evidence quality.

Techniques evaluated. All were single-shot ultrasound-guided fascial plane blocks: pectointercostal fascial block, transversus thoracis muscle plane block, erector spinae plane (ESP) block, and pectoralis nerve block type I (PECS I). Comparators were placebo (sham block) or no regional intervention, on top of standard general anesthesia and systemic analgesia.

Primary outcome: opioid consumption in the first 24 hours after surgery, expressed as morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Every regional technique significantly reduced 24-hour opioid consumption compared with placebo. In the network ranking, the ESP block was the most effective treatment, with a mean difference of -22.93 MME (95% confidence interval -34.29 to -11.56) versus placebo.

Secondary outcomes. Pain scores after extubation at 12 and 24 hours, postoperative nausea and vomiting, time to extubation, time to ICU discharge, and length of hospital stay were assessed. The direction of effect favored the regional techniques for analgesic outcomes, though the strength of evidence varied across outcomes.

Interpretation for practice. Fascial plane blocks reduce early postoperative opioid requirements after cardiac surgery with sternotomy. The analysis could not reliably determine which single technique is superior because few head-to-head trials exist; the authors call for more randomized controlled trials directly comparing techniques. Technique choice in practice therefore still depends on operator experience, patient anatomy, anticoagulation status, and institutional protocol rather than on proven superiority of one block.

Limitations. Small number of trials per technique, heterogeneity in block timing and local anesthetic regimens, and mostly surrogate analgesic outcomes rather than major morbidity endpoints. This summary condenses the published abstract and results; exact effect estimates for each pairwise comparison are in the full text.
title: Effects of ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia in cardiac surgery: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
